The exercises here use the 1,797 handwritten digits [@alpaydin1998optdigits]
and the center-ink [feature](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/course-overview.html#def-feature) from the [course overview](course-overview.qmd#sol-zero-or-one):
the average ink in rows 2 to 5 and columns 3 and 4 of each 8 by 8 image.
This chunk loads them again, with the left-ink feature from the same page.

```{python}
#| code-fold: false
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

digits = pd.read_csv("data/optdigits-test.csv", header=None)
pixels = digits.iloc[:, :64].to_numpy()
labels = digits[64].to_numpy()
images = pixels.reshape(-1, 8, 8)

center_ink = images[:, 2:6, 3:5].mean(axis=(1, 2))
left_ink = images[:, 2:6, 0:3].mean(axis=(1, 2))
print(images.shape, center_ink[:5], left_ink[:5])
```
